Native pointwise functional Gaussian random-intercept REML

etr_fit_functional_random_intercept_reml.Rd

Fits Gaussian random-intercept mixed models separately at each observed time using one-dimensional profiled restricted maximum likelihood. Repeated curves are grouped by participant. This is a native numerical method, not an exact port of the joint B-spline Python mixed-effects model.

Usage

etr_fit_functional_random_intercept_reml(trajectories, dimension,
  participant_column, design = NULL, predictors = character(),
  lambda_bounds = c(1e-08, 1e+06))

Arguments

trajectories

A complete finite native R trajectory set.

dimension

One named measurement channel.

participant_column

Metadata column identifying independent participant groups.

design

Optional one-row-per-curve data frame containing unique curve_id.

predictors

Character vector of declared numeric fixed-effect columns of design.

lambda_bounds

Finite increasing positive bounds for the nonzero variance-ratio optimization. Zero is always separately evaluated.

Value

An etr_functional_random_intercept_reml list with pointwise fixed coefficients and standard errors, participant BLUPs, residual and random-intercept variances, variance ratios, intraclass correlations, fitted functions, and conditional residuals.

Details

Model at each observed time is y_i = x_i beta + b_group(i) + error_i, with independent Gaussian group intercepts and errors. The restricted profile objective includes the determinant of the fixed-effects information matrix. No across-time covariance, random slope, or simultaneous inference is fitted. Boundary solutions are recorded.
